CvFormat.description: What the user uploaded. Only the extracted text is kept, never the file itself.
CvFormat.title: CvFormat

CvRead.description:
The caller's own CV. `text` is what was stored (emails, phones and links masked), so the
user can check exactly what the system holds.
CvRead.title: CvRead

CvSkillsWrite.description: The user's whole skills list (it replaces the stored one).
CvSkillsWrite.title: CvSkillsWrite

CvSuggestionsOut.description: Guesses read from the CV text. Shown to the user only: they never affect scoring.
CvSuggestionsOut.title: CvSuggestionsOut

MatchDetailOut.description: One match with its stored explanation.
MatchDetailOut.title: MatchDetailOut

MatchJobOut.description: The job as shown next to a score: public post fields only, no post text.
MatchJobOut.title: MatchJobOut

MatchPage.description: A page of matches, with the state of scoring so a client can say "updating".
MatchPage.title: MatchPage

PreferencesRead.description: The caller's saved preferences, or the empty defaults before anything was saved.
PreferencesRead.title: PreferencesRead

PreferencesWrite.description:
Everything the user wants, as one document: saving replaces what was stored.

A field left out means "no preference" for it. An empty list means any level / any policy.
PreferencesWrite.title: PreferencesWrite

SalaryPeriod.description: What the salary amounts of a post are per, exactly as the post states it.
SalaryPeriod.title: SalaryPeriod

ScoringOut.description: Whether the stored matches are current. Counters and a fixed code, nothing else.
ScoringOut.title: ScoringOut

SourceUpdate.description: Partial update: send only the fields to change. `type` cannot be changed.
SourceUpdate.title: SourceUpdate

SyncAcceptedOut.description:
The answer to "sync this source": the work was accepted, not finished.

The outcome shows up on the source (`last_synced_at`, `last_error`) and in `GET /jobs`.
SyncAcceptedOut.title: SyncAcceptedOut

delete.description: Delete your CV (its text included) permanently, and the matches ranked against it.

put.description:
Upload (or replace) your CV: send the PDF or plain text itself as the request body, with
`Content-Type: application/pdf` or `text/plain`. Only the text is kept, with emails, phone
numbers and links masked; the file is discarded. Uploading again replaces the CV and also
**discards any skills you edited** (they are read from the new text).

get.description:
Your skills (found in the CV, or the list you saved) and suggestions for years of
experience and seniority. The suggestions are only shown to you; nothing scores with them.
A CV stored before skills existed has an empty list until you save one or upload again.

put.description:
Replace your skills with this list. Names the dictionary knows are spelled its way.
Uploading a new CV later discards this list and reads the skills from the new text.
Your matches are scored again in the background.

get.description: Liveness check: returns 200 if the app is up. Does not touch the database yet.
Jobs collected from your sources, newest first. Optionally only those of one source.

post.description:
Try again to extract a job that failed or whose model step was given up on.

Returns 202: the extraction runs in the background and the result appears in `GET /jobs`.
`status` is `queued`, or `already_running` if a run is in progress (not an error). A job in
any other state gets 409 `not_retryable`; after 5 retries, 409 `retries_exhausted`. If the
queue is down the answer is 503 and nothing was changed. A retry does not skip the length
gate, the request budgets or the kill switch.

get.description:
Your jobs ranked for your CV, best first. The scores are the stored ones: reading never
recomputes, so while `scoring.state` is `pending` or `running` they may be a little behind.

A job that fails one of your hard filters (remote policy, seniority, salary) is hidden unless
you pass `include_filtered=true`. `source_id` limits the list to one of your sources.

post.description:
Ask for your matches to be scored again (the scores also refresh by themselves after a CV,
skills, preferences or job change). Returns 202: the run happens in the background; follow it
with `GET /matches/status`. `status` is `queued`, `already_pending` or `already_running`. No
CV: 404. If the queue is down: 503 and nothing was changed.

get.description: Is scoring finished? A cheap read of the state, for polling after a CV upload.

The stored explanation of one match. 404 when the job is not yours, does not exist, or has
no match yet (use `scoring` in the list to tell which).
Your saved preferences, or empty ones (`updated_at` is null) if you never saved any.

put.description:
Save your preferences. The body replaces what was stored: a field left out is cleared.
Your matches are scored again in the background.

delete.description: Delete a source **and all jobs collected from it**. Prefer `PATCH is_active=false`.

patch.description:
Change name, config and/or `is_active`. To stop fetching a source, set `is_active` to
false instead of deleting it.

post.description:
Ask for the source to be synced now. Returns 202: the sync runs in the background.

`status` is `queued`, or `already_running` if a sync of this source is in progress (not an
error: it is already fetching what you wanted). The result appears on the source
(`last_synced_at`, `last_error`) and in `GET /jobs`.
